articles.content:
Some 30 years ago Velran began it’s existence as a research outpost of the Merchant Republic of [[Amn]] , excavating ruins of the ancient Empire of [[Netheril]] . The discovery of elementally charged minerals however, buried in the soil and mountains of the surrounding area, quickly changed its fate. As the value of these minerals became apparent, savy merchants began pouring money into extensive mining operations, and the promise of riches lured thousands to the newly established town.

Ever keen on securing natural resources and expanding it’s influence, the Council of Six, ruling over Amn, quickly sent emissaries to claim the land, establish government structures and manage the construction of necessary infrastructure. Since then, plenty of smaller satelite-villages have been established around the area, providing mostly agricultural goods, making Velran less dependant on imports.

See also: [[Velran]]
articles.title: Velran (History)

articles.content:
Netheril was an ancient, magocratic human empire of Faerûn, whose influence was felt across the Realms for thousands of years. The Netherese people lived in a strict hierarchy for hundreds of years, split into the nobles of High Netheril, living in flying enclaves miles above Toril, and the commoners of Low Netheril settled in demesnes on the ground. During its glory years, the Empire of Magic would spread across a great stretch of Faerûn.

The empire was the pinnacle of human civilization during the first half of the Age of Humanity. Although they had humble roots as mere fishermen and farmers, the Netherese were introduced to the Art by the elves and came to harness this arcane power in ways that would shape Toril for generations. Over the next thousand years they discovered the long lost Nether Scrolls, developed the creation and use of mythallars and created the first of their flying citie. The arrogance of Netheril grew to the point where they attempted to attain the divinity of magic, and wound up killing the God of Magic and destroying the Weave (see [[Karsus's Folly]]. In the resulting maelstrom, the Faerûnian pantheon was altered and most of the flying cities of Netheril came crashing to the earth.
articles.title: Netheril
Karsus's Folly
articles.content: In −339 DR, the Magistocratic empire of [[Netheril]] ended with an event that came to be known as Karsus's Folly, an attempt by the brilliant arcanist Karsus to steal the power of the goddess of magic Mystryl and ascend to godhood. He cast an incredibly complicated, six-hour long spell of his own creation called Karsus's avatar, which finally tore apart the Weave, forcing Mystryl to sacrifice herself to keep it intact.

Wedged between the endless green Expanse of the [[Elfharrow Forest]] and the massive Mountains of the North Wall stands the proud city of Velran . Behind it’s impressive walls more than 30.000 souls have made their home in this bastion of civilization in the middle of nowhere.

# Life in the City
Life in Velran has been mostly peaceful since it’s establishment. The city itself is divided into different districts, with most of it’s inhabitants being craftsmen or public service provider. The government and residences of the wealthy merchant elite, are situated in a separate inner-city, on the highest part of the upwards sloping city inaccesible to most residents. In Velran, ‘moving up’ is often a very literal description. Outside of the massive outer walls, countless, mostly wooden buildings have sprung up where less successfull merchants, manual labourers and newcomers to the city have made their homes. Most buildings in the city proper are constructed from stone or half-timber and strongly resemble the architectural style of Amn despite the diversity of it’s inhabitants. The demographic composition of Velens citizens is more colorful than typical in the large cities of the west and it is not uncommon to see goblins, orcs and other species, often shunned in more ‘civilized’ places walking by without being given so much as a second glance.

# Outside of the City
The city is connected to the rest of civilization by a constant stream of caravans, bringing in goods and news from Amn and other places, and shipping off the precious minerals collected as well as the occasional artifact uncovered in the ruins of the ancient Netherese city, on whose remains Velran was built. Governor Von Wiedendorff who has been in charge of the city for the last 27 years has managed to established friendly relationships with a neighboring tribe of Dwarves ([[Barak'kor]]), making great use of their skill in the construction of the city, and managed to remain neutral to the nomadic tribes of elves inhabiting the forest despite initial conflicts. The occasional sightings of Fey: Sprites, dryads and other mysterious phenomena has become deeply ingrained in local folclore, but while it is not uncommon for mothers to threaten their children with child-stealing Fey, actual incidents regarding the reclusive denizens of the forest have so far remained more urban myth than real life danger.

The Commercial District Often just called "The Market" is the central district of the lowest plateau and home to the largest market place in Velran. Here Citizens and Travelers alike can find almost everything, at mostly competitive prices. Most of the Streets are lined with stores, both large and small. Once a week a large market on the the central plaza offers the frehest produce from the surrounding villages.

The Industrial District, colloquially referred to as "The Smokehouse" due to the smoke rising up from the smithies, produces most of the goods, being sold in the Commercial District. It is home to everything from tiny goldsmiths, to large warehouses with advanced manufactories. Apart from industry it is also home to several government offices like the post-office.

More than 1000 years ago [[Kossuth]], a powerful and destructive Fire Primordial broke through they veils that separate the Primordial Plane (our world) from the [[Prime Elemental Plane]]. A group of [[Netheril|Netherese]]Wizards, the 'Venerable Brothers of the Eternal Flame' thought to harness the might of primordial magic but ended up bringing death to thousands. After Kossuth, other Primordials emerged and either stood against him or took his side...

The confilct left the area a wasteland, the once majestic forest reduced to ash and nothing left but ruins of a proud and powerful enclave of Netheril.

Escape [one-action].description: You attempt to escape from being grabbed, immobilized, or restrained. Choose one creature, object, spell effect, hazard, or other impediment imposing any of those conditions on you. Attempt a check using your unarmed attack modifier against the DC of the effect. This is typically the Athletics DC of a creature grabbing you, the Thievery DC of a creature who tied you up, the spell DC for a spell effect, or the listed Escape DC of an object, hazard, or other impediment. You can attempt an Acrobatics or Athletics check instead of using your attack modifier if you choose (but this action still has the attack trait). [gold]Critical Success[/gold] You get free and remove the grabbed, immobilized, and restrained conditions imposed by your chosen target. You can then Stride up to 5 feet. [gold]Success[/gold] You get free and remove the grabbed, immobilized, and restrained conditions imposed by your chosen target. [gold]Critical Failure[/gold] You don't get free, and you can't attempt to Escape again until your next turn.
Escape [one-action].name: Escape [one-action]

Stride [one-action].description: You move up to your Speed
Stride [one-action].name: Stride [one-action]

Disarm [one-action].description: Requirements: You have at least one hand free. The target can't be more than one size larger than you. You try to knock an item out of a creature's grasp. Attempt an Athletics check against the target's Reflex DC. [gold]Critical Success[/gold] You knock the item out of the target's grasp. It falls to the ground in the target's space. [gold]Success[/gold] You weaken your target's grasp on the item. Further attempts to Disarm the target of that item gain a +2 circumstance bonus, and the target takes a –2 circumstance penalty to attacks with the item or other checks requiring a firm grasp on the item. The creature can end the effect by Interacting to change its grip on the item; otherwise, it lasts as long as the creature holds the item. [gold]Critical Failure[/gold] You lose your balance and become off-guard until the start of your next turn.
Disarm [one-action].name: Disarm [one-action]

Stand [one-action].description:
You stand up from prone. 

Standing up counts as moving for the purpose of effects such as Reactive Strike
Stand [one-action].name: Stand [one-action]

Create a Diversion [one-action].name: Create a Diversion [one-action]
Create a Diversion [one-action].description: With a gesture, a trick, or some distracting words, you can create a diversion that draws creatures' attention elsewhere. If you use a gesture or trick, this action gains the manipulate trait. If you use distracting words, it gains the auditory and linguistic traits. Attempt a single Deception check and compare it to the Perception DCs of the creatures whose attention you're trying to divert. Whether or not you succeed, creatures you attempt to divert gain a +4 circumstance bonus to their Perception DCs against your attempts to Create a Diversion for 1 minute. [gold]Success[/gold] You become hidden to each creature whose Perception DC is less than or equal to your result. (The hidden condition allows you to Sneak away) This lasts until the end of your turn or until you do anything except Step or use the Stealth skill to Hide or Sneak. If you Strike a creature, the creature remains off-guard against that attack, and you then become observed. If you do anything else, you become observed just before you act unless the GM determines otherwise. [gold]Failure[/gold] You don't divert the attention of any creatures whose Perception DC exceeds your result, and those creatures are aware you were trying to trick them.

Feint [one-action].name: Feint [one-action]
Feint [one-action].description: Requirements: You are within melee reach of the target you attempt to Feint. With a misleading flourish, you leave an opponent unprepared for your real attack. Attempt a Deception check against your target's Perception DC. [gold]Critical Success[/gold] You throw your enemy's defenses against you entirely off. The target is off-guard against melee attacks that you attempt against it until the end of your next turn. [gold]Success[/gold] Your foe is fooled, but only momentarily. The target is off-guard against the next melee attack that you attempt against it before the end of your current turn. [gold]Critical Failure[/gold] Your feint backfires. You are off-guard against melee attacks the target attempts against you until the end of your next turn.

[gold]Reach Spell[/gold] [one-action].name: [gold]Reach Spell[/gold] [one-action]
[gold]Reach Spell[/gold] [one-action].description: You can extend your spell’s range. If the next action you use is to Cast a Spell that has a range, increase that spell’s range by 30 feet. As is standard for increasing spell ranges, if the spell normally has a range of touch, you extend its range to 30 feet.

Shield Block [reaction].name: Shield Block [reaction]
Shield Block [reaction].description: Trigger: While you have your shield raised, you would take physical damage (bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing) from an attack. You snap your shield in place to ward off a blow. Your shield prevents you from taking an amount of damage up to the shield’s Hardness. You and the shield each take any remaining damage, possibly breaking or destroying the shield.

[gold]Fake Out[/gold] [reaction].description: Trigger: An ally is about to use an action that requires an attack roll, targeting a creature within your weapon's first range increment. Requirements: You're wielding a loaded firearm or crossbow. Fake Out does not require you to actually fire your weapon. With a skilled flourish of your weapon, you force an enemy to acknowledge you as a threat. Make an attack roll to [gold]Aid[/gold] the triggering attack. If you dealt damage to that enemy with the same weapon since the start of your last turn, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to this roll.
[gold]Fake Out[/gold] [reaction].name: [gold]Fake Out[/gold] [reaction]

Raise a Shield [one-action].name: Raise a Shield [one-action]
Raise a Shield [one-action].description: You position your shield to protect yourself. When you have Raised a Shield, you gain its listed circumstance bonus to AC. Your shield remains raised until the start of your next turn.

Demoralize [one-action].description: With a sudden shout, a well-timed taunt, or a cutting put-down, you can shake an enemy's resolve. Choose a creature within 30 feet of you who you're aware of. Attempt an Intimidation check against that target's Will DC. If the target doesn't understand the language you are speaking, or you're not speaking a language, you take a –4 circumstance penalty to the check. Regardless of your result, the target is temporarily immune to your attempts to Demoralize it for 10 minutes. [gold]Critical Success[/gold] The target becomes frightened 2. [gold]Success[/gold] The target becomes frightened 1.
Demoralize [one-action].name: Demoralize [one-action]

Interact [one-action].description: You can grab an unattended or stored object, open a door, etc.. You might have to attempt a skill check to determine if successful. This action generally provokes reactions such as Attack of Opportunity.
Interact [one-action].name: Interact [one-action]

Take Cover [one-action].description: Requirements: You are benefiting from cover, are near a feature that allows you to take cover, or are prone. You press yourself against a wall or duck behind an obstacle to take better advantage of cover. If you would have standard cover, you instead gain greater cover, which provides a +4 circumstance bonus to AC; to Reflex saves against area effects; and to Stealth checks to Hide, Sneak, or otherwise avoid detection. Otherwise, you gain the benefits of standard cover (a +2 circumstance bonus instead). This lasts until you move from your current space, use an attack action, become unconscious, or end this effect as a free action.
Take Cover [one-action].name: Take Cover [one-action]

Grapple [one-action].name: Grapple [one-action]
Grapple [one-action].description: Requirements: You have at least one free hand and your target is no more than one size larger than you. Attempt an Athletics check against the target's Fortitude DC. You can Grapple a target you already have grabbed or restrained without having a hand free. [gold]Critical Success[/gold] Your target is restrained until the end of your next turn unless you move or your target Escapes. [gold]Success[/gold] Your target is grabbed until the end of your next turn unless you move or your target Escapes. [gold]Failure[/gold] You fail to grab your target. If you already had the target grabbed or restrained using a Grapple, those conditions on the target end. [gold]Critical Failure[/gold] If you already had the target grabbed or restrained, it breaks free. Your target can either grab you, as if it succeeded at using the Grapple action against you, or force you to fall and land prone.

Burrow [one-action].name: Burrow [one-action]
Burrow [one-action].description: You dig your way through dirt, sand, or a similar loose material at a rate up to your burrow Speed. You can't burrow through rock or other substances denser than dirt unless you have an ability that allows you to do so.

Fly [one-action].name: Fly [one-action]
Fly [one-action].description: You move through the air up to your fly Speed. Moving upward (straight up or diagonally) uses the rules for moving through difficult terrain. You can move straight down 10 feet for every 5 feet of movement you spend. If you Fly to the ground, you don't take falling damage. You can use an action to Fly 0 feet to hover in place. If you're airborne at the end of your turn and didn't use a Fly action this round, you fall.

Long Jump [two-actions].description: You Stride, then attempt a DC 15 Athletics check to make a long jump in the direction you were Striding. If you didn't Stride at least 10 feet, you automatically fail your check. The GM might increase or decrease this DC depending on the situation. [gold]Success[/gold] You Leap up to a distance equal to your check result rounded down to the nearest 5 feet. You can't jump farther than your land Speed. [gold]Failure[/gold] You make a normal horizontal Leap. [gold]Critical Failure[/gold] You make a normal horizontal Leap, then fall and land prone.
Long Jump [two-actions].name: Long Jump [two-actions]

Bon Mot.description: You launch an insightful quip at a foe, distracting them. Choose a foe within 30 feet and roll a Diplomacy check against the target's Will DC. [gold]Critical Success[/gold] The target is distracted and takes a –3 status penalty to Perception and Will saves for 1 minute. The target can end the effect early with a retort to your Bon Mot. This can either be a single action that has the concentrate trait or an appropriate skill action to frame their retort. The GM determines which skill actions qualify, though they must take at least 1 action. Typically, the retort needs to use a linguistic Charisma-based skill action. [gold]Success[/gold] As critical success, but the penalty is –2. [gold]Critical Failure[/gold] Your quip is atrocious. You take the same penalty an enemy would take had you succeeded. This ends after 1 minute or if you issue another Bon Mot and succeed.
Bon Mot.name: Bon Mot

Shove [one-action].name: Shove [one-action]
Shove [one-action].description: Requirements: You have at least one hand free. The target can't be more than one size larger than you. You push a creature away from you. Attempt an Athletics check against your target's Fortitude DC. [gold]Critical Success[/gold] You push your target up to 10 feet away from you. You can Stride after it, but you must move the same distance and in the same direction. [gold]Success[/gold] You push your target back 5 feet. You can Stride after it, but you must move the same distance and in the same direction. [gold]Critical Failure[/gold] You lose your balance, fall, and land prone.

Strike [one-action].name: Strike [one-action]
Strike [one-action].description: You attack with a weapon you’re wielding within its given range. If you critically succeed on the attack roll, you deal double damage*.

Step [one-action].description:
You carefully move 5 feet. Unlike most types of movement, Stepping doesn't trigger reactions, such as Reactive Strike, that can be triggered by move actions or upon leaving or entering a square.

You can't Step into difficult terrain, and you can't Step using a Speed other than your land Speed.
Step [one-action].name: Step [one-action]

Leap [one-action].description: You take a short horizontal or vertical jump. Jumping a greater distance requires using the Athletics skill for a High Jump or Long Jump. [gold]Horizontal Jump[/gold]up to 10 feet horizontally if your Speed is at least 15 feet, or up to 15 feet horizontally if your Speed is at least 30 feet. You land in the space where your Leap ends (meaning you can typically clear a 5-foot gap, or a 10-foot gap if your Speed is 30 feet or more). You can't make a horizontal Leap if your Speed is less than 15 feet. [gold]Vertical Jump[/gold] up to 3 feet vertically and 5 feet horizontally onto an elevated surface.
Leap [one-action].name: Leap [one-action]

Trip [one-action].description: Requirements: You have at least one hand free. Your target can't be more than one size larger than you. You try to knock a creature to the ground. Attempt an Athletics check against the target's Reflex DC. [gold]Critical Success[/gold] The target falls, lands prone, and takes 1d6 bludgeoning damage. [gold]Success[/gold] The target falls and lands prone. [gold]Critical Failure[/gold] You lose your balance, fall, and land prone.
Trip [one-action].name: Trip [one-action]

Crawl [one-action].description: While you are prone, you are unable to Stride or Step. Instead, you Crawl 5ft (if speed is more than 5ft).
Crawl [one-action].name: Crawl [one-action]

activities.effectCrit: You find the perfect spot for a camp. Flat checks to determine encounters at the campsite for the next 24 hours have a DC 2 higher than normal, and the Foraging DC is 2 lower than usual.
activities.effectFail: Your campsite will work, but it's not the best. Campsite activities that require checks take a –2 penalty.
activities.name: Prepare Campsite
activities.effectCritFail: The campsite is a mess. You can use it to rest and to perform daily preparations, but it isn't good enough to allow for Campsite activities at all. Worse, your attempt to secure a campsite has possibly attracted unwanted attention—attempt a flat check against the zone's Encounter DC. If successful, a random encounter automatically occurs.
activities.description: You spend 2 hours searching the hex for a safe and secure location to make camp and then setting up the campsite itself by attempting a Survival check against the Zone DC of the region you're located in. Once a campsite is prepared, you can use the Prepare Campsite activity in this same Area again in the future (but no more than once per 24 hours) to automatically achieve the same degree of success with only an hour of work.
activities.effectSuccess: You find a serviceable spot for a camp and for Camping activities. No bonus or penalties.

activities.description: You help organize Camping activities to be more efficient, allowing the campers to attempt additional Camping activities during the camping session. Attempt a Survival check against the Zone DC to determine how helpful your management is.
activities.effectSuccess: As critical success, but only you and one other PC may attempt two Camping activities during the session.
activities.name: Camp Management
activities.effectCritFail: Your plans backfire, resulting in inefficiencies during the rest of the camping session. All checks made to resolve Camping activities take a –2 circumstance penalty for the remainder of this camping session.
activities.effectCrit: Your advice speeds things along significantly. During the Camping-Session, each PC may attempt two Camping activities instead of one. This success does not increase the number of activities companions may attempt.
activities.effectFail: Your management is neither particularly helpfull nor hindering. No Bonuses or Penalties apply.

activities.effectCrit: You grant your ally a +2 circumstance bonus to the activity. If you're a master with the check you attempted, the bonus is +3, and if you're legendary, it's +4.
activities.effectFail: You Fail to help your ally, no bonus but no penalties either.
activities.description: You take 2 hours to aid another character in their Camping activity. When you Provide Aid, attempt a skill check of a type decided by the GM. The typical DC is 15, but the GM might adjust this DC for particularly hard or easy tasks. You can Provide Aid as many times as you want during a camping session, but remember that the circumstance bonuses granted by Provide Aid do not stack.
activities.effectSuccess: You grant your ally a +1 circumstance bonus to the activity's check.
activities.name: Provide Aid
activities.effectCritFail: Your ally takes a –1 circumstance penalty to their activity's check.

activities.description: You spend your time concealing the camp from potential threats by covering tents with branches, ensuring campfire placement minimizes the spread of scent or smoke, reminding others to avoid making too many loud noises, and so on. Attempt a Stealth check against the Zone DC. You can only attempt to Camouflage Campsite once per camping session, regardless of the activity's result.
activities.effectSuccess: Your work helps hide your camp from detection. Increase the Encounter DC for your camp by 2.
activities.effectCritFail: You believe you've done well at your camouflage attempt but have actually forgotten something important or accidentally did something to make the campsite more noticeable. Decrease the Encounter DC for your camp by 2, and flat checks made to determine encounters result in a critical success on a roll of 19 or 20.
activities.name: Camouflage Campsite
activities.effectFail: Your camouflage falls flat and does nothing to hide your camp. No bonuses or penalties.
activities.effectCrit: Your camouflage attempt exceeds expectation. Increase the Encounter DC for your camp by 4.

activities.description: You spend your time to take the lead on organizing the camp's watch rotation, optimizing shifts, and scouting the surrounding area to determine which approaches to the camp are most likely to be used by enemies. Attempt a Perception check against the Zone DC.
activities.effectSuccess: You discover excellent scouting positions. Characters gain a +1 status bonus to Perception checks made during their shift on watch.
activities.name: Organize Watch
activities.effectCritFail: As failure, but you may have attracted unwanted attention. Attempt a flat check against the zone's Encounter DC to determine if a random encounter occurs.
activities.effectCrit: The camp's watch is efficient and your scouting setup immaculate. Treat the total time required for rest as if the party size were 2 more, and all characters gain a +2 status bonus to Perception checks made during their shift on watch.
activities.effectFail: Your attempt to organize the watch doesn't grant any additional benefits or penalties.

activities.effectSuccess:
You prepare a decent meal. 
A character who eats this meal recovers Hit Points equal to their Constitution modifier (minimum 1) multiplied by twice their level when they rest during this camping session instead of the normal amount. 
They also gain a +1 status bonus to all saving throws until they complete their daily preparations and a +1 bonus to the first saving throw they make the following day.
activities.description:
You spend your time preparing a meal. Expend 2 basic ingredients per serving you wish to prepare, as well as 1 day's rations, or provisions from Subsisting, per serving.

Once the party finishes all Camping activities and the characters have chosen which meals they wish to eat, attempt a DC 22 Survival check or a DC 18 Cooking Lore check to determine the effectiveness of your basic meal.
activities.name: Cook Basic Meal
activities.effectCritFail: Your meal wreaks havoc on digestion. A character who partook of this meal becomes sickened 1 until after they rest and complete their daily preparations.
activities.effectCrit:
You prepare a delicious meal. 
A character who eats this meal recovers Hit Points equal to their Constitution modifier (minimum 1) multiplied by twice their level when they rest during this camping session instead of the normal amount. 
The characters start the next day with Temporary HP equal to their Constitution modifier * level/2 or equal to their level, whchever is higher.
They also gain a +1 status bonus to all saving throws until they complete their daily preparations and a +1 bonus to the first saving throw they make the following day.
activities.effectFail: Your meal fills bellies, but has no other effects.

activities.description:
You spend time preparing a special meal. Choose a special meal whose recipe the party knows and then expend the basic and special ingredients required for each serving you wish to prepare, as well as 1 day's rations, or provisions from Subsisting, per serving. Special meal recipes are formulas you can purchase at a settlement or discover on your own with the Discover Special Meal activity.

Special meals also count as basic meals, The effects of Cook basic meal apply in addition to the specific effects of the chosen meal.

You can cook multiple servings in one Cok Special meal action.
Cook Special Meal can be attempted multiple times during a camping session, using a different recipe.

A character who is sickened can't eat a special meal or gain its benefits.

Once the party finishes all Camping activities and the characters have chosen which meals they wish to eat, attempt a Survival check or a Cooking Lore check to determine the effectiveness of your special meal. The DC of the check required varies by recipe. Unless the special meal's description says otherwise, its effects last until the next time the party prepares a camp or 24 hours, whichever comes first.
activities.effectSuccess:
You follow the recipe to the letter.
The character gains the recipe's listed success effect.
A character who eats this meal recovers Hit Points equal to their Constitution modifier (minimum 1) multiplied by twice their level when they rest during this camping session instead of the normal amount. 
They also gain a +1 status bonus to all saving throws until they complete their daily preparations and a +1 bonus to the first saving throw they make the following day.
activities.effectCritFail:
You botch the recipe and create a health hazard, barely disguised as food.
The character suffers the recipe's critical failure effect.
A character who partook of this meal becomes sickened 1 until after they rest and complete their daily preparations.
activities.name: Cook Special Meal
activities.requirements: Trained in Survival or Cooking Lore
activities.effectFail:
You try to follow the recipe but something went wrong.
The character gains no special benefit from the meal, though it still prevents starvation.
activities.effectCrit:
You surpass the original recipe, improvising on the spot to create a masterpiece.
The character gains the recipe's listed critical success effect.
A character who eats this meal recovers Hit Points equal to their Constitution modifier (minimum 1) multiplied by twice their level when they rest during this camping session instead of the normal amount. 
The characters start the next day with Temporary HP equal to their Constitution modifier * level/2 or equal to their level, whchever is higher.
They also gain a +1 status bonus to all saving throws until they complete their daily preparations and a +1 bonus to the first saving throw they make the following day.

You discover the special meal and add it to the list of recipes the party knows. 
In addition, your research was efficient, and you recover half of the ingredients you had to expend to attempt this activity.
activities.effectFail: You fail to discover the special meal and do not recover any ingredients.
activities.description: You spend your time attempting to discover a special recipe. Choose a common recipe; the recipe must be of a level equal to or less than the level of the zone you're camping in. Expend twice the normal amount of ingredients required to prepare 1 serving of the special meal, then attempt that special meal's Cooking Lore check.
activities.effectSuccess: You discover the special meal and add it to the list of recipes the party knows
activities.name: Discover Special Meal
activities.effectCritFail:
You fail to discover the special meal and do not recover any ingredients.
You also expose yourself to the special meal's critical failure effect while performing an unwise taste test.

Reach Spell.description: You can extend your spells’ range. If the next action you use is to Cast a Spell that has a range, increase that spell’s range by 30 feet. As is standard for increasing spell ranges, if the spell normally has a range of touch, you extend its range to 30 feet.
Reach Spell.name: Reach Spell

Sorcerous Potency.name: Sorcerous Potency
Sorcerous Potency.description: Because of the magical power inherent in your blood, your spells that hurt or cure are stronger than those of other spellcasters. When you Cast a Spell from your spell slots that either deals damage or restores Hit Points, you gain a status bonus to that spell's damage or healing equal to the spell's rank. This applies only to the initial damage or healing the spell deals when cast. An individual creature takes this damage or benefits from this healing only once per spell, even if the spell would damage or heal that creature multiple times.

Munitions Crafter.name: Munitions Crafter
Munitions Crafter.description: You can use the advanced alchemy benefits to create a number of daily consumables equal to 4 + half your level (rounded up); these consumables must be bombs or alchemical ammunition. You create the ammunition in batches of 4

Fake Out.description: Trigger: An ally is about to use an action that requires an attack roll, targeting a creature within your weapon's first range increment. Requirements: You're wielding a loaded firearm or crossbow. Fake Out does not require you to actually fire your weapon. With a skilled flourish of your weapon, you force an enemy to acknowledge you as a threat. Make an attack roll to [gold]Aid[/gold] the triggering attack. If you dealt damage to that enemy with the same weapon since the start of your last turn, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to this roll.
Fake Out.name: Fake Out

Natural Medicine.description:
You can apply natural cures to heal your allies. You can use Nature instead of Medicine to Treat Wounds, including higher Nature proficiency letting you attempt more difficult checks. It doesn’t replace Medicine for uses of the skill other than Treat Wounds or for feat prerequisites.

If you’re in the wilderness, you might have easier access to fresh ingredients, allowing you to gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your check to Treat Wounds using Nature, subject to the GM’s determination.
Natural Medicine.name: Natural Medicine

Combat Climber.description: Your techniques allow you to fight as you climb. You’re not offguard while Climbing and can Climb with a hand occupied. You must still use another hand and both legs to Climb.
Combat Climber.name: Combat Climber

Crafter's Appraisal.description: Your knowledge of items' construction allows you to discern their magical effects as well. You can use Crafting instead of a skill associated with a magic tradition to Identify Magic on magic items, though not on any other sorts of magic.
Crafter's Appraisal.name: Crafter's Appraisal

Quick Alchemy.description: You can create up to 4 versatile vials during your daily preparation. You can use up a versatile vial to make another alchemical consumable at a moment's notice. Any effect created by an item made with Quick Alchemy that would have a duration longer than 10 minutes lasts for 10 minutes instead. Create Consumable [one-action]: You expend one of your versatile vials to create a single alchemical consumable item of your level or lower that's in your formula book. You don't have to spend the normal monetary cost in alchemical raw materials or need to attempt a Crafting check. This item has the infused trait, but it remains potent only until the start of your next turn. (As normal, you need only one formula for an item to create any level of that item.)
Quick Alchemy.name: Quick Alchemy

Ash-Piercing Gaze.name: Ash-Piercing Gaze
Ash-Piercing Gaze.description: Neither cinders nor winds shall prevent you from seeing those who need help. You automatically succeed at the flat check to target a concealed creature if that creature is concealed only by smoke or mist.

Unbowed, Unbroken.name: Unbowed, Unbroken
Unbowed, Unbroken.description:
Your connection to elemental wood manifests as resilience—towering trees, rough bark, deep roots, and patient determination. You gain the Unwavering Resilience reaction.

Unwavering Resilience [reaction] Trigger You attempt a saving throw against a poison, disease, or mental effect, but you haven’t rolled yet. EffectYou tap into the power of the Plane of Wood, gaining strength and mental fortitude. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus on the triggering save. If you critically succeed at this saving throw, you become bolstered by your success; blossoms and new growth temporarily sprout all over your body, and you gain a number of temporary Hit Point equal to your level. These temporary Hit Points last for one minute. When there temporary Hit Points are lost, the verdant growth subsides.

Burn it!.description: Your spells and alchemical items that deal fire damage gain a status bonus to damage equal to half the spell's rank or one-quarter the item's level (minimum bonus +1). You also gain a +1 status bonus to any persistent fire damage you deal.
Burn it!.name: Burn it!

Blood Magic.name: Blood Magic
Blood Magic.description:
Casting a sorcerous gift spell granted by your bloodline or a bloodline spell allows you to benefit from a blood magic effect you know. You can typically only benefit from one blood magic effect at a time, though some feats and abilities may change this.

Elemental Fury Elemental energy wreathes your form and infuses your magic. Either you gain a +2 status bonus to Intimidation checks for 1 round, or a target takes 1 damage per spell rank; this damage type is listed under your elemental influence. If the spell already deals that type of damage, combine it with the spell's initial damage before determining weaknesses and resistances.

description.value: Blood-drinking vines grow from the ground in a 15-foot burst within 120 feet. Each living enemy in the area has its blood drained, taking 4d6 piercing damage with a basic Fortitude save against DC 22. Each time the vines drink blood, living creatures in the area who aren't your enemies regain HP equal to half the damage a single creature took; calculate this using the highest damage a single creature took. The vines last until the end of your next turn, and you can Sustain the impulse. The first time you Sustain the impulse on subsequent turns, you can repeat the effect.

The Aspect of Immortality can choose whether or not it takes vitality damage.

Thorny vines grow in geometric patterns on surfaces in the creature's kinetic aura. A creature that starts its turn in the thorns takes a –10-foot circumstance penalty to its Speeds until it leaves the area. The thorns are hazardous terrain. A creature takes 3 piercing damage each time it moves into one of these squares. If any square the thorns grow on is water or soil, double the hazardous terrain damage for all thorns. If you move, the thorns disappear; new thorns grow at the end of your turn.

A haze of pollen floats around you. A creature in your kinetic aura when you enter the stance, or who later enters the aura or ends its turn in the aura, attempts at a Fortitude save against DC 22. On a failure, it's sickened 1 (sickened 2 on a critical failure) and dazzled until it's no longer sickened. A creature attempts this save no more than once per round and doesn't attempt a new save if already affected.

A long vine sprouts from your arm, which you can temporarily wield like a whip. Make a melee attack roll against a creature within 20 feet. If you succeed, the vine deals 3d6 slashing damage, or double damage on a critical success.

Awakening The vine coils around your foes, squeezing them lifeless. On a successful hit, the target is grabbed by the vine. The DC to Escape the vine is 22. Each round on your turn, if the target is still grabbed, the vine squeezes them, dealing 3d6 bludgeoning damage.
Awakening Rather than lash at your foes with a single vine, dozens of writhing vines emerge from your hands, lashing all creatures in a large area. You can use Vine Lash as a 2-action activity to damage all creatures in a 30-foot cone, with a basic Reflex save.
This Creatureis nigh unkillable. The Creature gains resistance against all damage equal to its level (minimum 3), and it gains weakness equal to twice its level (minimum 6) to critical hits.

You grow a shield of woven flowers and branches, then Raise that Shield to defend yourself from the triggering attack. If you would take damage from the attack, you immediately Shield Block. This is a wooden shield. The shield remains in your possession for a number of rounds equal to your level, or until it’s destroyed.

Awakening The shield becomes stronger. It has Hardness 5, HP 40, BT 20.
Awakening The shield takes on a mind of its own and lashes out vengefully when destroyed. When the shield is destroyed, is explodes, dealing 4d6 piercing damage to your attacker, with a basic Reflex save.

You unleash the rot infecting you, spreading the blight to those nearby. All living creatures in a 60-foot emanation take 1d6 void damage for every 2 levels you have, with a basic Fortitude save.

Awakening The blight is infectious. Creatures damaged by your blight take an additional 1d6 persistent void damage, as they begin to decompose.
Awakening The blight is debilitating. Creatures damaged become drained 1 for one round on a success, drained 1 for 1 minute on a failure, and drained 2 for 1 minute on a critical failure.

custom-1776170493104.description: The creature collects elemental matter from it's aura and swings or hurls it. It  makes a melee or ranged impulse attack against the AC of one creature. It adds it's Strength modifier to the damage roll for a melee Elemental Blast. If it makes a 2-action Elemental Blast, it gains a status bonus to the damage roll equal to it's Constitution modifier.
custom-1776170493104.name: Elemental Blast

awakening2.name: Forest of Vines [two-actions]
awakening2.description: Rather than lash at your foes with a single vine, dozens of writhing vines emerge from your hands, lashing all creatures in a large area. You can use Vine Lash as a 2-action activity to damage all creatures in a 30-foot cone, a 60 ft line or a 15ft emanation with a basic Reflex save. The Area turns into difficult terrain for 1 round per 2 levels you have.

vine_lash_one_action_1776780987695.name: Vine Lash [one-action]

awakening1.name: Grasping Vine  [one-action]
awakening1.description: The vine' s range increases to 60 ft. It coils around your foes, squeezing them lifeless. On a successful hit, the target is grabbed by the vine. The DC to Escape the vine is equal to your Class DC or Spell DC, whichever is higher. Each round on your turn, if the target is still grabbed, the vine squeezes them, dealing 1d6 bludgeoning damage for every 2 levels you have.

vine_lash_one_action_1776780987695.description: A long vine sprouts from your arm, which you can temporarily wield like a whip. Make a melee attack roll against a creature within 30 feet. If you succeed, the vine deals 1d6 slashing damage for every 2 levels you have to the target, or double damage on a success.

release_spores_two_actions_1776781870590.name: Release Spores [two-actions]

awakening2.name: Rejuvenating Spores  [two-actions]
awakening2.description: The Spores glitter and smell like flowers. The miasma grants Quick healing x , x being equal to half your level , to allies who begin their turn in the area, and to allies who enter the area.

release_spores_two_actions_1776781870590.description: You create a miasma of spores. These spores fill a 20-foot burst within 100 feet and remain for 1 round per level you have. All creatures within the spores become concealed, and all creatures outside the spores become concealed to creatures within it. You can see through the spores without difficulty. You can Dismiss the spores.

awakening1.name: Poisonous Spores  [two-actions]
awakening1.description: The Spores are poisonous. The miasma deals 1 poison damage per level you have to creatures in the area when you Release Spores, to creatures who begin their turn in the area, and to creatures who enter the area. Creatures  in the area are sickened 1 for as long as they remain in the area, plus 2 rounds. You are exempt from the miasma's effect yourself.

apostle_of_the_briar_1776783165756.description: You have been invested with a fragment of the Wood-Primordial's Power. You can feel the energies of Life and Nature pulsing through your veins....and maybe just a hint of corruption...
apostle_of_the_briar_1776783165756.name: Apostle of the Briar

severe.description: You become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.Fatigued] for the rest of the day and become@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.Sickened] 4. The sickened condition reduces by 1 per hour but cannot be reduced by any other means.

moderate.description: You become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.Fatigued] and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.Sickened] 2  until you spend 20 minutes recuperating by resting and doing nothing. If you spend this time basking in sunshine, it instead takes 10 minutes.

mild.description: You become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.Fatigued] 1 as the plants feed off your life force. This condition lasts until you spend 3 consecutive actions to rest and do nothing
